thread:
Maria P: Heads-up — we had sustained queueing in us-west-2 cluster for ~10m, queues jumped to ~85% of capacity and the warm pool didn't fill quickly enough. Rolling logs attached. Need quick sync on reserve vs ephemeral split and a safe mitigation to stop token-bucket blowouts.
Kevin L: Can you paste the alert details? curious about scale-up latency and prealloc time.
Maria P: ops-bot posted it, but short summary: high_queued_requests=423, avg_scale_up=34s, prealloc_delay=18s, warm_pool_fill_pct=9% :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
ops-bot: ALERT us-west-2-gpu-pool high_queue_rate=210/s queued=423 prewarm_gap_s=18 scale_action="scale_up_delayed"
Ash (eng-infra): Looks like a double-provision hit — ephemeral (spot) instances taking 20-40s to attach + our prealloc_timeout is only 10s. Warm pool target at 10% isn't cutting it for bursty traffic.
Samira: Quick mitigation: increase warm_pool_target_percent to 25% and prealloc_timeout_ms to 12000. Also enable leaky-bucket admission with refill_rate=500 tokens/s, burst=1500. That should smooth spikes without immediate overprovision.
Lucas R: 25% warm pool will increase baseline cost. What's the estimated monthly delta? we need numbers to sign off for today.
Samira: Rough calc: ~6 GPUs extra in us-west-2 steady = +$6k/mo. Compare that to lost-SLO risk — 85% queueing caused 12% request latency tail increase, potential customer impact.
Elaine: Can we do a safer experiment: increase warm pool to 18% and set permissive leaky-bucket (refill 400/s, burst 1200) + a canary route for non-critical tenants? If green, bump to 25%.
Kevin L: +1 to canary. Also reduce prealloc_timeout to 60s? Wait we want longer timeout to avoid killing in-progress prealloc. Set prealloc_timeout_ms=60000.
Ash (eng-infra): Prealloc timeout 60s is long but prevents churn. However we should also cap ephemeral scale rate to 3 nodes/min to avoid rapid spot churn. Proposed admission change: max_inflight_per_gpu=16, admission_window_ms=250, token_bucket={refill=400,burst=1200}.
Maria P: I'll push a small change set to configmap and trigger a canary in us-west-2-b. Plan: step1: warm_pool_target_percent=18, prealloc_timeout_ms=12000, token_refill=400/burst=1200; step2: monitor 15m; step3: if queueing <30% and tail latency down -> bump to 25 and reduce token refill to 500.
Kevin L: Please include rollout runbook. If queueing worsens, rollback within 10m and re-evaluate.
Samira: Runbook snippet:
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: autoscaler-config
data:
  warm_pool_target_percent: "18"
  prealloc_timeout_ms: "12000"
  token_refill_per_s: "400"
  token_burst: "1200"
  max_ephemeral_scale_per_min: "3"
EOF
```
Samira: Monitor metrics: queued_requests, avg_scale_up_s, warm_pool_fill_pct, tail_p99_latency, spot_reclaims. Alert if queued_requests > 200 for 5m.
Lucas R: Okay on canary, but parallel ask finance to pre-approve temporary bump to 25% if canary goes green. I'll cc finance.
Maria P: Action items: Samira deploys canary -> Ash watches node attach logs -> Kevin monitors admission metrics -> Lucas loops finance -> Elaine approves canary route. I'll post results in 15m. :ok_hand:
ops-bot: RUNBOOK: canary_deploy started by Samira at 1841239999
Samira: canary applied to us-west-2-b at 1841239999
Ash (eng-infra): seeing prealloc attach jitter down to ~9-14s, warm pool filled to 19% within 3m. queued_requests trending down.
Maria P: Early numbers look promising. Will update after 15m. Thanks team!
